question.prompt:
Points \(F,\) \(G,\) and \(H\) are collinear with \(G\) between \(F\) and \(H.\) The ellipse with foci at \(G\) and \(H\) is internally tangent to the ellipse with foci at \(F\) and \(G,\) as shown below.

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_12A_Q14_question_fig1.svg)

The two ellipses have the same eccentricity \(e,\) and the ratio of their areas is \(2025.\) (Recall that the eccentricity of an ellipse is \(e = \dfrac{c}{a},\) where \(c\) is the distance from the center to a focus, and \(2a\) is the length of the major axis.) What is \(e?\)

solutions.explanation:
Equal eccentricity gives the ellipses the same shape, so their area ratio will first give a length ratio. Let \(A>a>0\) be the major semiaxes of the ellipses with foci \(F,G\) and \(G,H\), respectively. Their common eccentricity satisfies \(0<e<1\), and
\[
FG=2eA,\qquad GH=2ea.
\]
An ellipse with major semiaxis \(a\) consists of points whose distances to its two foci sum to \(2a\). Scaling the smaller ellipse by \(A/a\) makes its focal separation \(2eA\) and its distance sum \(2A\). After placing its foci at \(F,G\), it is exactly the larger ellipse. Thus the ellipses are similar, and
\[
\left(\frac{A}{a}\right)^2=2025,
\qquad \frac{A}{a}=45.
\]
We next turn tangency into a focal distance equation. For any point \(P\) on the smaller ellipse, \(PG+PH=2a\). The direct segment from \(F\) to \(P\) is no longer than the path through \(H\), so
\[
PF+PG\le FH+PH+PG
=2e(A+a)+2a.
\]
This bound is attained at the smaller ellipse's right major-axis endpoint: because \(a>ea\), that endpoint lies beyond \(H\), making the path from \(F\) through \(H\) to \(P\) straight.

Points inside or on the larger ellipse satisfy \(PF+PG\le2A\), with equality on its boundary. Containment and contact therefore require the maximum just found to equal \(2A\). Hence
\[
2A=2e(A+a)+2a,
\]
so, using \(A+a>0\),
\[
e=\frac{A-a}{A+a}
=\frac{45-1}{45+1}
=\frac{22}{23}.
\]
This is between \(0\) and \(1\), as required. The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{22}{23}}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Focal distance sums and area scaling
Use equal-eccentricity similarity and prove the axis contact
